observations.statement: synypokrinomai (G4942, 'to join hypocrisy') in its one occurrence -- Peter's withdrawal at Antioch causing 'the rest of the Jews' to 'act hypocritically along with him,' drawing in Barnabas too. Morph V-API-3P (aorist passive/middle indicative, 3rd plural) -- a group subject, not an individual.

The word's own compound structure (syn- 'together with' + hypokrinomai 'play a hypocrite') makes hypocrisy here inherently relational rather than a private inconsistency: LSJ's own gloss is 'accommodate oneself by pretending... helping [another] maintain his pretence.' The single occurrence is exactly this -- one person's (Peter's) hypocrisy spreading by imitation to a group, then to a specific named third party (Barnabas). This is a social-contagion structure, not an individual moral failure examined in isolation.

This social-contagion structure matches the pre-existing (legacy, pre-2026-06-25-reset) M10 characteristic 'Contagious sin' (characteristic.id=31, 'sin as a moral direction set by a leader... transmitted to those under their authority') and the independently-found Jeroboam causative-sin formula in family B_sin (H2398, 'made Israel to sin'). Three separate pieces of evidence -- one legacy characteristic, one lexical family, and this one -- converge on the same pattern: sin/hypocrisy propagating through a leader-follower relationship rather than occurring in one person alone.

This family has exactly one strong and one occurrence -- the thinnest possible evidence base for a distinct family. Worth the same explicit low-confidence flag as L_defilement: a single data point cannot be triangulated against itself for alternative readings the way multi-occurrence strongs can.
